Avec environ 40 000 hectares brûlés, l’incendie qui a ravagé le département est devenu l’un des plus vastes feux de forêt jamais enregistrés en France, et même en Europe. Le réchauffement climatique favorise ces incendies hors norme qui se multiplient.

En Gironde, « la crise n’est pas finie, le feu n’est pas fixé, mais on progresse », a déclaré la préfète Sophie Brocas. Quels sont les plus grands feux de forêt en France depuis 1975 ? Avec environ 42 000 hectares brûlés depuis le 22 juillet, les incendies en Gironde dépassent de loin les plus grands feux de forêt répertoriés ces dernières décennies.

Plusieurs points chauds persistent autour du Cap-Ferret et de Lacanau.

« Les régions les plus sensibles au risque d’incendie sont aussi celles où l’artificialisation des sols a le plus progressé » La Gironde, en proie à un mégafeu depuis le 22 juillet, a vu une partie importante de sa forêt reculer au profit des habitations au cours du temps. Une modification du territoire qui a pu augmenter le risque d’incendie, et la difficulté pour les pompiers de combattre le feu, analyse, dans un entretien au « Monde », la géographe Christine Bouisset.

La cellule de crise regroupe tous les services impliqués dans le sinistre. Jeudi 30 juillet au soir, les points chauds étaient moins nombreux.

Nuñez, précisant que « le retour des habitants ne pourra se faire que progressivement ».

Ils y voient le symptôme d’une Europe rattrapée par les effets du changement climatique.

Quelque 3 300 sapeurs-pompiers sont toujours mobilisés dans le département, ainsi que 1 500 militaires, 1 250 policiers et gendarmes et 24 moyens aériens. Les pompiers en Gironde se disent « raisonnablement optimistes » après une nuit calme.

officialCheckpoints.detail: Lacanau’s official 11:50 point says campsites and holiday residences can reopen, with local bus links including Bordeaux–Lacanau and Canéo services expected to resume normally from Saturday 1 August.

officialCheckpoints.detail: The town hall says the communal situation is stable and the fire is no longer progressing, but it remains active in the forest and dune south-east of Grand Crohot, with substantial resources deployed. This keeps Cap Ferret in cautious staged-recovery rather than normal visitor-access mode.

officialCheckpoints.title: Prefecture point · 16:00
officialCheckpoints.detail: The prefecture’s 30 July 16:00 point is retained as the official bridge between the first re-entry wave and the broader staged-recovery picture now visible around the Bassin and Lacanau.

officialCheckpoints.title: Nine communes re-integrated; A63 reopened
officialCheckpoints.detail: The prefecture’s 30 July release records re-entry in nine communes and the reopening of the A63, the first major official shift from evacuation/access blockage toward staged regional recovery.

officialCheckpoints.title: Cars and TER still disrupted
officialCheckpoints.detail: The regional transport homepage says cars in Gironde and Landes are interrupted or heavily disrupted by the fires, and TER traffic is interrupted between Bordeaux and Arcachon and between Bordeaux and Morcenx.

officialCheckpoints.title: Lège-Cap-Ferret point · 12:00
officialCheckpoints.detail: The town hall says the local situation is stable but still concerning, firefighters are handling flare-backs, the forest remains under surveillance, conditions are expected to deteriorate from the evening, no return to the peninsula is possible until further notice, and forest-defence work includes a new firebreak near L’Herbe.

officialCheckpoints.title: Lège-Cap-Ferret official point
officialCheckpoints.detail: The municipal point says flare-ups continue around Lège Bourg and Claouey under surveillance, the Claouey Sud firebreak widening is nearly finished, and the rest of the peninsula shows no fire evolution for now.

officialCheckpoints.title: NASA thermal detections · 24h
officialCheckpoints.detail: TVCapFerret added a 14:46 view of the last-24-hour NASA FIRMS detections, showing recent thermal activity across a wide perimeter rather than a real-time fire-front map.

officialCheckpoints.title: Prefecture point · 13:00
officialCheckpoints.detail: The 13:00 prefectural baseline reports 42,000 hectares burned, nearly 220,000 people evacuated in 23 communes, 240 homes destroyed, 75 firefighters treated and major routes including parts of the A63 still affected.

officialCheckpoints.title: Arès mayor point · 10:30
officialCheckpoints.detail: TVCapFerret links the 10:30 Arès mayor update as a local operational checkpoint for conditions around the north Bassin evacuation area.

officialCheckpoints.title: Le Porge point and impact map · 08:00
officialCheckpoints.detail: The Le Porge point says the night was relatively calm locally, crews worked overnight, 152 damaged homes were listed by the mairie, and the village remained closed.

officialCheckpoints.title: Trains interrupted
officialCheckpoints.detail: Rail traffic is listed as interrupted between Bordeaux and Arcachon and between Bordeaux and Morcenx, with cancellations expected during 26 July.

officialCheckpoints.title: NASA thermal map · 06:53
officialCheckpoints.detail: The morning thermal comparison showed newer detections extending south-east, with the peninsula still under watch because older detections and wind shifts could remain relevant.

officialCheckpoints.title: Closed roads · map
officialCheckpoints.detail: TVCapFerret’s quick-access trail points readers to the road-closure map, which should be checked against Gironde Inforoutes before inferring any road is open.

officialCheckpoints.title: Reception centres · 04:00
officialCheckpoints.detail: A 04:00 checkpoint lists reception-centre capacity and reinforces the scale of preventive evacuations away from the fire area.

officialCheckpoints.title: Prefecture point · 02:00
officialCheckpoints.detail: The overnight prefectural point is retained as the first official 26 July checkpoint in this trail, useful for detecting later changes in totals, access and instructions.
